source.title: Finding Transformer Circuits with Edge Pruning
source.authors: Adithya Bhaskar; Alexander Wettig; Dan Friedman; Danqi Chen

page_placements.theme: Discovery implementation changes circuit faithfulness and size

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a different, learned edge-pruning method to evaluate how faithfully sparse circuits reproduce GPT-2 IOI behavior, and compares circuit faithfulness across methods and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper tests its own circuits on IOI, including a 30-template version, but does not inspect or intervene on the original 26-head circuit or test the roles of its named head classes. Its IOI method comparisons and faithfulness evaluations bear on V5. IOI-t1 is also evaluated, but the paper does not test whether one circuit or mechanism carries IOI across prompt variants. Other reported tasks and CodeLlama Boolean Expressions do not bear on these claim versions. Figures 2, 3, and 5 include sparsity-sweep results; rows below summarize only outcomes stated in the text where individual plotted values are not stated.
record.test_reason: Mostly a method paper: IOI serves as a benchmark for comparing Edge Pruning with ACDC and EAP. One result bears on a version. Appendix B (Figure 7) compares the IOI circuits found automatically with the manually found circuit, using node ROC curves over attention heads (AUC 0.8256 for Edge Pruning vs 0.8108 for ACDC). This is a direct test of whether other methods recover the same circuit (V4). No row records it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. Also: the authors find Edge Pruning matches ACDC on overlap with the manual IOI circuit. They stress that manual circuits are not guaranteed optimal and recommend faithfulness metrics over overlap metrics.
record.recipe_differences: The original IOI circuit was manually reverse-engineered and assessed through targeted interventions. This paper learns edge masks with gradient-based pruning and evaluates circuits using interchange ablation, chiefly by KL divergence and task performance.
record.method_sensitivity: On multi-template IOI, reported KL results vary substantially among ACDC, EAP, and Edge Pruning at similar sparsity. The paper separately evaluates single-template IOI-t1 and multi-template IOI; it describes Edge Pruning as competitive on IOI-t1 and especially strong on multi-template IOI. Secondary Exact Match results are said to echo the main faithfulness comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched 96.6% sparsity, the KL faithfulness of automatically found IOI circuits varies widely by method (EAP 3.47–3.78, ACDC 0.88–0.92, Edge Pruning 0.20–0.25).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How faithful an automatically discovered IOI circuit is depends strongly on the discovery method.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 12 seeds, the pairwise edge IoU of Edge Pruning IOI circuits is about 0.52–0.64, while their KL stays consistent (about 0.27–0.30).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Several distinct, equally faithful edge-level circuits can implement IOI in GPT-2 small, so the circuit is not unique.

record.problems: The IOI method comparisons report faithfulness results for circuits found by the paper's methods, not the original 26-head circuit. Most method-comparison values are shown in sparsity-sweep figures rather than reported numerically in the text. The paper's checklist states that it does not report error bars or statistical significance for the main comparisons; the ±0.1 figure in Table 1 is for sparsity.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 2, 3, and 5 show additional sparsity-sweep points and task-performance/faithfulness curves. The text gives qualitative summaries but not individual numeric values for those points, so they are not separately extracted beyond the summarized figure/text results in R9-R11.

untested.parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality are never evaluated directly.
No ablation of name-mover heads and no measure of backup heads; Appendix C only remarks that circuits may miss backup components.
No IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints.
Recovery of edges, head classes and roles, and comparison across ablation types for the IOI circuit. Only node-level overlap over attention heads is tested.
No variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution applied to the claimed circuit.
No test that the same components carry IOI across name orders or templates.

missing.what: Node ROC overlap of IOI circuits with the manual Wang et al. circuit (attention heads only): AUC 0.8256 for Edge Pruning vs 0.8108 for ACDC.
Seed consistency of IOI circuits: IoU 0.52–0.64 across 12 seeds at a 97.5% target sparsity.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted rows benchmark circuit-finding methods on circuits each method finds itself, so they do not evaluate the claimed 26-head circuit and are relinked to none. The only result bearing on a version is the Figure 7 overlap comparison (V4), which needs a row.

versions.untested_parts: The specific 26 attention heads, seven classes, their stated roles, and the faithfulness, completeness, and minimality of that particular circuit.
The paper does not ablate the main name-mover heads and measure whether backup heads take over. Its general note about circuits potentially missing backup components is not a test of this version.
No IOI circuit is tested across other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks for reuse of the stated head classes and roles.
Although it compares circuit-finding methods, it does not test whether they recover essentially the same head classes or roles as the claimed circuit, nor compare ablation types for that circuit.

It compares circuit-finding methods and reports alternate metrics and IOI prompt sets, but does not vary ablation type on the claimed circuit or establish how much of the original 26-head circuit's behavior it explains.
IOI-t1 and multi-template IOI are evaluated separately, but the study does not establish that the same circuit or head roles carry behavior across name orders, templates, or more names.
